body: This introduces a render-phase state update to mirror the `errors` prop (`setPrevExternalErrors` / `setErrors` inside the render body). Render-phase updates can behave poorly under Strict Mode / concurrent rendering and are generally discouraged; previously this was handled in an effect (`useValueChanged`). Consider syncing `externalErrors` to local `errors` state in an effect (with a ref comparison) instead of calling state setters during render.
This test creates a `vi.spyOn(...)` but never restores it. In this repo, spies are typically `mockRestore()`'d (often in a `finally`) to avoid leaking a spied prototype method into later tests.

Keeping this as-is. React documents this exact conditional, same-component state adjustment as preferable to an Effect when a prop changes: https://react.dev/learn/you-might-not-need-an-effect#adjusting-some-state-when-a-prop-changes. React retries the component before rendering children or committing the DOM, and the identity guard makes the update converge under Strict Mode. Moving it back to an Effect would commit once with stale external errors.
Fixed in 013344b6d by restoring the prototype spy in a `finally` block, including when the test fails.
